transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-31
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Jordan, Nina (Redwood); Alan, Priya, Sven, Leah (BridgePoint)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intro round, then Jordan will walk through the staging plan and we'll capture network/security asks.
[00:27] Alan (BridgePoint): Hey all, Alan here. We're looking to get BridgePoint's first on-prem-ish deployment live in September, so tight timeline. We've got DevOps and security on the line here.
[00:40] Priya (BridgePoint): Priya, DevOps. Main constraint is we can't open broad egress from our subnets; egress rules need to be approved by infra. Also need to confirm data residency for logs.
[00:52] Maya: Got it, thank you. Nina from CSM will own cadence. Jordan, over to you for the staging and perf outline.
[01:05] Jordan (Redwood SE): Cool, thanks. I'll try to keep it practical — staging -> canary -> prod. Stage 1 is VPC connectivity and API smoke tests, Stage 2 is feature canary (embedding + chat paths), Stage 3 is load test and rollout. We'll instrument cost/latency dashboards in the console.
[01:28] Priya: When you say VPC connectivity, do you mean VPC peering or VPN? We have a transit gateway setup.
[01:37] Jordan: Either works; peering or transit. We typically do VPC peering for low-latency calls but can do private link if you need AWS TGW. We'll share a network diagram and sample security group rules. Link: https://redwood.example.com/deck/bridgepoint-network.
[01:56] Sven (BridgePoint): Security — we require SOC 2 plus ISO audition — sorry, ISO 27k, and we need proof of key rotation and audit logs. Also KMS into HSM is a hard ask.
[02:09] Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, and we can integrate with HSM providers via key wraps. I'll put the KMS integration notes in the runbook. Note: some minor transcription typo earlier - it's K V cache, not K V cash — ha.
[02:28] Alan: (laughs) — good to know. On SLAs, what's Redwood's target p95 for single-turn chat on Dedicated?
[02:36] Maya: For Dedicated we publish p95 numbers around 250-450ms for 512-token sequences on xG models; larger context increases linearly. We'll include model/seq length breakdown in the performance appendix.
[02:52] Leah (BridgePoint): We're planning some 8k prompts for re-ranking flows, curious about tail latency there.
[02:58] Jordan: Yeah larger sequences and KV cache misses will push tails. We'll run a 20k token sequence benchmark for your workloads — sequence distribution and cache warm/cold scenarios. I want your representative prompt set.
[03:14] Priya: We'll sanitize and share 10 sample prompts and a traffic shape doc. Question: does Redwood's prefix caching work across tenants? We run multitenant in prod.
[03:25] Jordan: Good question. Prefix/KV caching is per-namespace/tenant by default. We can tune TTLs and shard caching policies — will note in the runbook.
[03:36] Speaker 7: [inaudible]...
[03:41] Maya: Let's go through the network intake checklist — Priya, we need CIDRs for peering, outbound allowlist for the private control plane, and your proxy/SNAT patterns.
[03:52] Priya: I can pull those; I'll need a sample allowlist template.
[03:57] Maya: We'll send one. Also, for SSO, do you use SAML with Okta?
[04:03] Alan: Yes, Okta, and SAML. We also use SCIM for provisioning.
[04:08] Nina (Redwood CSM): We have an SSO setup guide and SCIM mapping examples, I'll share both.
[04:15] Sven: On audit logs — we need immutable delivery to our SIEM. Can Redwood forward audit events to an S3 bucket or log collector?
[04:25] Jordan: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we can stream audit logs to your s3 or syslog collector. There is also in-console logs and a configurable retention. We'll detail retention and encryption in transit and at rest in the docs.
[04:40] Alan: Good. Also curious on failover — if a Dedicated pool has degradation, what's the fallback path?
[04:48] Maya: We can configure policy-based routing: fallback to a compatible hosted variant, or route to a lower-cost quantized model. That behavior is configurable per-route with canary rules.
[05:00] Priya: Any data egress concerns when fallback hits hosted? We need to keep data in our VPC for compliance.
[05:07] Maya: For BridgePoint we'll recommend a private-only policy for sensitive routes — no automatic external fallback unless you explicitly opt-in.
[05:16] Leah: Timeline — we want staging by mid-August, canary late August, prod early September. Is that realistic?
[05:24] Jordan: Yes, with fast approvals for network and SSO. Main gating items: VPC peering, KMS contact, and perf benchmark results.
[05:33] Maya: Let's capture owners on that.
[05:36] [10:12] 
[10:12] Jordan: Quick demo segment — walking through the console runbook view and observability. (screen share noises, short pause) 
[10:40] Jordan: Here you can see route-level token cost, per-model latency heatmaps, and the rollout control for canary percentages.
[11:02] Leah: Can we get token-level billing exported to our billing system?
[11:08] Jordan: Yes, we expose per-token billing CSVs and have a billing API you can hit. We'll provide the schema.
[11:20] Priya: For the benchmark, can you simulate our traffic shape: 70% short prompts <256 tokens, 25% 1-2k, 5% long form 8k+?
[11:31] Jordan: Absolutely, include that in the traffic doc. We'll run cold and warm cache runs.
[11:39] Alan: Security process — procurement needs our legal/regulatory checklist. Who do we send to?
[11:46] Maya: Send it to procurement@redwood.com and CC Nina. We'll share our SOC 2 attestation and ISO 27k docs in the security pack.
[11:57] Sven: Any PII concerns in logs? We want to ensure transcripts aren't stored beyond retention.
[12:03] Maya: Retention policies are configurable and we can redact or disable transcript storage for certain routes. That will be in the playbook.
[12:12] Priya: There's also egress VPN — we'd like mutual TLS for control plane calls. Is that standard?
[12:19] Jordan: mTLS for control plane is supported for Private installs; we'll list cert rotation and bootstrap steps.
[12:27] Leah: For RBAC mapping, can we sync Okta groups to Redwood roles?
[12:33] Nina: Yes, SCIM group-to-role mapping is supported, we'll include sample mapping files.
[12:39] Alan: Pricing — will there be a separate Dedicated sizing estimate?
[12:45] Maya: We'll provide a sizing and cost estimate based on your expected qps and token volume. That will be in the follow-up collateral with a few scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive).
[12:57] Speaker 3: [overlap]... I have one more question about quantization and accuracy tradeoffs.
[13:03] Jordan: We can run a quantized candidate for cost-savings on non-critical routes. Redwood Optimize will recommend quant profiles based on your eval set; we'll show quality delta on the same prompt set.
[13:18] Priya: Ok. We'll need a simple A/B plan for quality checks during canary.
[13:23] Maya: We'll include an eval harness template — you can plug in your golden prompt set.
[13:28] Alan: Nice. Anything else on the network side?
[13:33] Priya: One last ask — certificate pinning for egress endpoints?
[13:38] Jordan: Supported. We'll add fingerprint rotation docs.
[13:44] Nina: I'll take notes on the calendar cadence. Weekly standup Tuesdays at 10am PT?
[13:49] Priya: Works for me.
[13:52] Maya: Great. Recap of owners: Maya will send runbook + SSO guide; Jordan will own perf plan; Priya and Sven will provide infra and compliance contacts; Nina will schedule recurring invites.
[14:05] Alan: Anything else?
[14:08] Leah: Clarify the demo access — do you provide a sandbox account for product team?
[14:12] Jordan: Yes, we can provision a sandbox namespace with sample data. We'll give Leah access once we have SSO mapping or temporary creds.
[14:21] Maya: Ok we're at the last five minutes — any blockers?
[14:25] Priya: No blockers, just need the allowlist template.
[14:29] Maya: We'll send immediately after the call.
[14:33] Nina: I'll send meeting notes and the invite for weekly Tuesday 10am PT.
[14:38] Alan: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the runbook.
[14:41] Maya: Thanks, appreciate it. End meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: some overlap and inaudible short segments around 03:36 and 10:12 due to screen-share audio. Certain tech terms slightly garbled in auto-transcript (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash").
